function.name: get_boiling_melting_points
function.description: Retrieve the boiling point and melting point of a substance based on its name and the sea level. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Wait "海平面下5000米處" could mean "at 5000 meters below sea level" (i.e., undersea depth). But typical context: "海平面下5000米處" might refer to "5000 meters below sea level" which is deep ocean. But we need to interpret: They want boiling point and melting point of water at 5000 meters below sea level. That is unusual because water under high pressure will have higher boiling point. But also melting point may shift slightly.

We can use the function get_boiling_melting_points with substance "water" and sea_level 5000? But the function expects sea_level in meters. It says "Retrieve the boiling point and melting point of a substance based on its name and the sea level." So we pass sea_level=5000. But the function likely expects sea_level relative to sea level? Actually sea_level parameter is the sea level in meters. So if we want 5000 meters below sea level, we might pass sea_level=-5000? But the function expects sea_level in meters. It might accept negative values. But the description: "the sea level in meters" ambiguous. Usually sea level is 0 at sea level. So if we want 5000 meters below sea level, we pass -5000. But the function might not handle negative. But we can try.

Alternatively, maybe they want at 5000 meters above sea level? But phrase "海平面下5000米處" literally means "5000 meters below sea level". So we pass sea_level=-5000.

But the function might not support negative. But we can still call it.

Let's call the function with substance="water", sea_level=-5000.
